title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-19 14:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE), Sara Huang (Redwood CSM); Dana Rivers (Orbital Health CTO), Miguel Santos (Infra), Anya Patel (Security), Tom Reed (ML Eng), Elena Park (Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed networking progress (VPC peering, route tables), recent infra upgrade window, routing/NAT issues affecting model access, benchmark results (latency P50/P95), and next steps: security doc handoff, test plan for canary upgrade, and follow-up benchmark run after routing fix.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'll kick us off, um quick agenda - networking status, infra upgrades, perf results from last week, then open issues and next steps
[00:21] Dana: thanks jordan, appreciate it, we've got a hard stop at 2:45 so try keep to the agenda
[00:27] Priya: quick intro, i'm priya from redwood se focusing on private deployment plumbing; liam will jump in on perf and sara on ops
[00:35] Miguel: on our side miguel, infra lead, been wading through the route table stuff since last Wednesday
[00:41] [00:45] Tom: tom here, ml eng, i'll be running the benchmark jobs and sharing logs

[01:10] Priya: ok networking first â€” last week we saw the peering established but some subnets weren't propagating routes, that was the NAT gateway vs transit gateway mismatch, can you confirm miguel if the propagations are enabled now?
[01:27] Miguel: yes we enabled propagation on the tgw but we noticed the route table for the model subnets was missing the 10.2.0.0/16 entry, that was me â€” i forgot to attach the rt to the private subnet, fixed that yesterday
[01:44] Anya: quick sec, are we still using customer-managed KMS for key wrapping? security needs that confirmed before we run canary with real data
[01:58] Jordan: yes, that's our default for private deployments â€” we support CMKs via the customer's KMS, priya can confirm the integration path
[02:10] Priya: confirmed, we mounted the key via the keystore plugin and the redwood private agent talks to the remote kms over mutual TLS, there was one cert mismatch which caused handshake failures in the earlier run
[02:30] [02:35] Miguel: that was me again, the cert chain from our internal CA wasn't including the intermediate; fixed and validated last night

[03:00] Liam: on the model runtime â€” we pushed a small kernel selection update to the private runtime on tuesday to improve fp16 quant path, overall P50 improved a bit but P95 spiked on long prompts
[03:18] Tom: yeah saw that in the logs, P50 ~ 85ms, P95 ~ 420ms for the 2k token job. we suspect the cache warming is inconsistent when the request routing goes through the transit path vs local subnet
[03:36] Priya: that aligns with our hypothesis â€” cross-AZ traffic causes KV cache misses and serialization overhead, which explains the P95 tail

[04:05] Jordan: show of hands, anyone still blocked from running the notebook benchmark?
[04:12] Elena: we have intermittent 502s when the request hits the LB that routes to the private agent, mostly during burst loads
[04:22] Sara: noted; we did see LB health check flaps in the logs earlier, likely because the agent restarted when it couldn't reach the KMS endpoint (cert issue patched)

[05:00] Tom: i ran three runs overnight, baseline run1, run2, run3 â€” attached notes in the shared folder link (see deck link in calendar). run1 had sticky sessions which helped latency, run2 had round robin which exposed cold cache
[05:19] Jordan: (laughs) classic sticky vs rr debate â€” we can advise on session affinity for the canary window

[05:40] [05:45] Miguel: routing question â€” we have a NAT in the private subnet for egress to S3. Should redwood agent be allowed egress via NAT or do you recommend a VPC endpoint?
[05:55] Priya: we prefer VPC endpoints for S3 when possible to avoid NAT scaling issues and to keep egress within aws backbone; also it's easier for policy/audit logs
[06:10] Anya: can you add note about logs â€” we need audit-level access for KMS calls and S3 putobject events in our retention window
[06:20] Jordan: yes we'll provide a mapping of which operations need to be logged and how to turn on enhanced audit in your environment

[06:45] Liam: perf deep dive â€” i instrumented the runtime and found that the latencies correlate with two things: (1) first-token generation after a cache miss, (2) occasional CPU contention on the agent host when the quant kernels run fallback paths
[07:10] Tom: interesting, our host metrics show CPU spikes at the same timestamps as the P95 spikes
[07:18] Liam: so two mitigations: increase agent host CPU share or pin the runtime to a different kernel selection for long prompts; second is to enable local KV prefetch for frequently used prompt prefixes

[07:45] Miguel: how invasive is the kernel pin? would it require an restart/outage?
[07:52] Priya: small restart of the agent process, we can do a rolling restart with zero downtime if you have at least two agent replicas per subnet â€” which you should for high availability

[08:15] [08:20] Jordan: regarding upgrades, we plan a canary for next Tuesday during the midnight window, need to confirm maintenance window with orbital infra
[08:29] Miguel: midnight works but we need a rollback plan; last time the commit changed kernel flags and we had to revert which took 45 minutes
[08:36] Priya: we'll provide a pre-baked rollback script and a health-check that fails the upgrade if P95 increases beyond threshold

[09:05] Anya: about compliance docs â€” can you resend SOC 2 and ISO artifacts? we already have an NDA so we can ingest redwood artifacts into our doc repo
[09:15] Jordan: yes i'll push the security pack to the shared drive after the call, includes SOC2 type II, ISO audit summary, KMS integration guide, and agent hardening checklist

[09:40] Tom: a small note on model artifacts â€” the model tar is ~6.2GB compressed, we are pulling from our S3 via a signed URL; in the earlier attempt the download stalled and the agent retried which caused duplicate partial files
[09:57] Priya: we have anatomic resume support and a lockfile to prevent partial-file collisions; sounds like the agent didn't have write permissions to /var/repo during that run
[10:10] Miguel: permissions were defaulted to ec2-user; we missed the chown step in the bootstrap script, updated the IaC yesterday to set correct owner

[10:40] Liam: metrics wise â€” after the fix, the warm-start P50 is 70ms, P95 180ms for 512-token prompts, but for 2k prompts P95 still ~420ms on cross-AZ hits
[11:05] Tom: do we have telemetry to map which requests cross AZ?
[11:12] Priya: yes the agent emits a routing tag we can correlate with AZ header; we'll produce a synthetic trace to show the distribution

[11:30] [11:35] Elena: product question â€” what's the rollback impact on ongoing sessions? our UX team worried sessions might be dropped mid-generation
[11:42] Priya: rolling restarts preserve session tokens; we drain new connections and let in-flight token generation finish before a pod restarts

[12:05] Jordan: ok open issues list â€” (1) confirm canary window and rollback plan, (2) finalize VPC endpoints and NAT removal plan, (3) audit log retention config, (4) fix LB health check flaps and agent restarts, (5) run another benchmark after routing fix

[12:25] Tom: quick question â€” can we try a micro-batching config? our workload has many short prompts and batching could improve throughput and cost without hurting latency too much
[12:38] Liam: yes micro-batching with dynamic timeout 10ms helped reduce token cost by 8% in our internal tests; we can propose a conservative profile for you to test

[12:55] Anya: and on security again, SAML SSO mapping â€” we need RBAC roles to map to our internal groups for prod pilot
[13:05] Jordan: we'll share the SSO integration doc and a sample role-mapping YAML, also confirm whether you want group sync via SCIM

[13:30] Miguel: is there any dependency on external IP allowlisting for the agent to reach redwood control plane? we want to lock down egress strictly
[13:40] Priya: only if you opt into the hosted control plane; for private you can disable the control-plane callback and we operate via a customer-managed control plane in your VPC â€” then egress to public internet is not required

[14:02] [14:05] Jordan: last part â€” next steps and responsibilities
[14:12] Jordan: i'll send the security pack and the canary runbook, priya will send kernel pin instructions and batching profile, liam will drop perf traces, and miguel will confirm endpoint changes
[14:25] Dana: sounds good, can we get the next sync same time next week?
[14:30] Jordan: same time next week works â€” i'll send calendar invite

[14:40] Miguel: thanks everyone, appreciate the help â€” we'll aim to flip the VPC endpoint on monday and run a small smoke test
[14:45] Jordan: great, meeting adjourned
